Billet aluminum engine covers

Engine covers and automotive housings for prototype fitment and small-batch projects.

Start with the cover perimeter and underside clearance as well as the visible billet contour and finish.

Request a quote

From 1 piece · 7–14 business days
From drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing; transit is additional.

Materials & manufacturing
Part features
Sweeping 3D curves, mounting interfaces and visible machining textures.
Made to order
Made to your approved drawing and quotation, including the material, dimensions and acceptance criteria. Not a stock item.
More views of the part geometry

Reference views for comparing shape, interfaces and surface features. Confirm the geometry and requirements of your own part with a controlled drawing.

Original reference photograph of a curved cover and its visible tool-path texture.
Materials & manufacturing
Quality and inspection
About this example

Use the photo to compare the shape and features with your part. It does not specify the alloy, dimensions or inspection results.

Materials and finish options

Choose the material and finish for your application. The options below are available for custom orders; they are not confirmed specifications of the photographed part.

6061-T6 or 7075 billet engine covers with 5-axis curves and ball-nose toolpath textures.
Prototype and small-batch support includes checking hood, camshaft and sensor clearances.
Materials
6061-T6 aluminum, with 7075 as an alternative.
Machining
5-axis machining from solid billet, with optional polishing, brushing or anodizing.
Finish options & requirements
Polishing, brushing and anodizing.
Applications
Custom engine covers and automotive development parts.
Prototype Machining
Aluminum CNC Parts
CNC Milling Service
5 Axis CNC Machining
Low Volume Production
Drawing & inspection checklist

A billet cover needs engine-bay clearance and a specified finish on visible surfaces.

Fitment and clearance checks appear in the catalog notes. Agree the dimensional inspection plan for your cover.

Drawing details

Locate mounting holes and the mating perimeter from assembly datums; show underside clearances and local wall sections.

Inspection checks

Agree mating-face, mounting-pattern and clearance checks, with separate appearance acceptance for the outer contour.

Requesting a quote

Provide the mating envelope, alloy and temper, finish requirements and whether any seal interface is present.

Underside clearance and seal interfaces

Define the underside as well as the visible cover contour. Show fastener access and clearance to adjacent parts. If the cover uses a gasket or seal, provide the interface and mating-face requirements; the photograph cannot define them.

Visible finish and masked fits

Mark cosmetic faces and areas where tool-path texture is acceptable. Specify the anodized or polished finish and supply an appearance reference if available. Before accepting a finish proposal, agree how to check masked fits and finished dimensions.

01
Drawing and specifications

Before quoting, we review the drawing, critical dimensions, mating surfaces, material and finish to agree the inspection plan.

02
Sample inspection

Review the sample inspection results with us and resolve drawing changes before approving production.

03
Checks during production

We inspect the first article and check agreed features during manufacturing against your order requirements.

04
Final inspection and shipment

Final QC takes place before shipment, using the acceptance criteria and records agreed for your order.

See the complete manufacturing process
Inspection methods
for your order

Match the measurement method to the dimensions, datums and acceptance requirements on your drawing.

Ask us to supply current calibration records for your supplier review.

Coordinate measuring machine
Positions and geometric features, checked against drawing datums.
Height gauges
Heights and dimensional checks using the agreed setup.
Optical projectors
Profiles and features suited to optical measurement.

Mark any critical tolerances on your drawing. We assess them against the material and part geometry, then confirm the setup and measurement method. For selected features, ±0.01 mm may be a useful engineering reference after review, but it is not a general tolerance or guarantee. Ask us to confirm the instrument range and supply current calibration evidence. We also need to confirm which measurement records can be provided for your order.

See machining and inspection equipment

to the feature

Start with the drawing feature and its acceptance limits, then agree the instrument, setup and record needed for the order.

Dimensions & fit
Identify mating diameters, lengths and thread requirements. Discuss suitable dimensional tools and gauges for those features.
Heights, profiles & geometry
Define the datum system and the relationships between features. Confirm the setup and whether height, optical or coordinate measurement is appropriate.
Surface & material checks
If roughness, coating thickness or hardness matters, state the method and acceptance criteria. Confirm which checks and records can be supplied.

for your order

Identify critical features and the first-article or dimensional report format you need. Specify the datums and whether dimensions apply before or after finishing.
